name: Johanan
overview: Johanan was a male descendant of the tribe of Ephraim noted in Scripture as the father of Azariah. His significance lies in his familial connection to Azariah, who played a role in aiding the defeated Judaites. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond this relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means 'YHWH has been gracious,' reflecting a common theophoric element expressing God's grace. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful acknowledgment of divine kindness.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Johanan as the father of Azariah, highlighting a direct paternal relationship. He is also explicitly noted as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim. Beyond these, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's importance in the biblical narrative is primarily through his son Azariah, who actively assisted the Judaites after their defeat, indicating a role of support and restoration during a time of crisis. This connection situates Johanan within the broader context of intertribal interactions and the ongoing history of Israel's tribes during challenging periods.
